column4: Visit note | 2025-08-03 02:00 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Mostafa Islam, 51, male. Mr. Islam presents for his first visit complaining that he has been looking notably pale and getting breathless on the stairs. He explains that his symptoms started after a stomach illness during a stay in Sirajganj a few weeks ago. He works as a mobile phone repair technician, sitting for long hours in his shop in Dhaka, and has felt unusually fatigued during his working hours. He reports no history of bleeding gums, blood in stools, or other major chronic illnesses. He takes no regular prescription medications. On examination, his vital signs and investigations reveal: haemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, BP 134/79 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 61 kg. He appears pale on inspection, but his chest is clear to auscultation and heart sounds are normal without murmurs. Abdominal examination is unremarkable with no palpable organomegaly. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued for iron replacement therapy and supportive agents. He was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid tea within an hour of meals to improve iron absorption. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.
